**Majority of Europe's largest banks now monetise premium APIs beyond compliance**

*A Salt Edge study finds 58% of major European banks offer commercial API products, reshaping competitive dynamics as PSD3 and FIDA negotiations determine the boundary between mandated and voluntary data sharing.*

Salt Edge has published new data showing that 58% of Europe's largest banks now offer premium API services beyond the access mandated by PSD2. The figure marks a shift from the early years of open banking, when most banks treated API provision as a compliance obligation with no commercial upside.

The report suggests that banks are extending their open banking foundations to support more complex financial and treasury use cases, including account aggregation, payment initiation for corporate clients and data-enrichment services sold to third parties. The trend reflects a broader pattern: as the regulatory baseline matures, the competitive question is no longer whether banks comply, but whether they can build a commercial layer on top of the infrastructure they were required to create.

For fintechs and third-party providers, the growth of premium APIs creates both opportunity and complexity. Richer data and functionality improve what can be built, but commercial terms vary widely across banks and markets, and standardisation remains limited. As PSD3 and the Financial Data Access regulation (FIDA) move through the legislative process, the interplay between mandated and voluntary data sharing will shape how this market develops.

*Sources: [Beyond Compliance: Why 58% of Europe's Largest Banks Now Offer Premium APIs](https://financialit.net/news/open-banking/beyond-compliance-why-58-europes-largest-banks-now-offer-premium-apis) — Financialit | [New Salt Edge report explores the commercial potential of premium APIs](https://www.openbankingexpo.com/news/new-salt-edge-report-explores-the-commercial-potential-of-premium-apis/) — Openbankingexpo | [58% of Europe's Largest Banks Now Monetize Premium Open Banking APIs Beyond PSD2 ...](https://ffnews.com/news/new-data-58-of-europe-s-largest-banks-now-monetise-open-banking-apis-beyond-psd2-cfa8e046) — Ffnews*

**Payconiq to Wero migration gets firm dates in Luxembourg**

*Luxembourg users will begin downloading the Wero app from September 7, as EPI's rollout extends to its sixth European market with a phased transition from Payconiq.*

Wero is set to launch in Luxembourg on September 7, when the app will become available for download across the country, marking the European Payments Initiative's expansion into its sixth market. The rollout follows a phased approach, with some existing Payconiq users migrating earlier and others gaining access on the launch date.

The transition from Payconiq to Wero in Luxembourg follows a similar pattern to the migration underway in the Netherlands, where iDEAL is being folded into Wero's infrastructure. Luxembourg's relatively small market makes it a lower-risk deployment, but the migration tests EPI's ability to replace established national payment brands — a challenge that will intensify as Wero enters larger and more fragmented markets.

Person-to-person payments will be the initial use case, consistent with Wero's launch strategy in Germany, France, Belgium and the Netherlands. Online merchant payments are expected to follow, though timelines for commercial acceptance in Luxembourg have not been confirmed.

*Sources: [From Payconiq to Wero: what changes and when in Luxembourg?](https://www.luxtimes.lu/businessandfinance/some-wero-users-will-have-to-wait-a-week-longer-to-download-the-app/160424210.html) — Luxtimes*

**Visa joins Singapore-led project to pilot stablecoin settlement**

*Participation in a government-backed pilot to connect traditional payment rails with stablecoin networks extends a pattern of major schemes positioning for tokenised settlement.*

Visa is joining a project led by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to pilot settlement across traditional payments infrastructure and stablecoin networks. The initiative aims to test interoperability between conventional clearing systems and token-based value transfer — a question that is becoming increasingly practical as stablecoin volumes grow and regulatory frameworks such as MiCA take effect.

Visa's involvement follows a series of moves by the major card networks into stablecoin infrastructure. Mastercard added stablecoin settlement to its merchant network in June, and both schemes have been expanding their roles in tokenised payment flows. For Visa, the Singapore pilot complements its existing work on USDC settlement through Circle and its broader push into programmable money.

The MAS has positioned Singapore as a testing ground for tokenised financial infrastructure through its Project Guardian and related initiatives. The convergence between stablecoin settlement pilots in Asia and the regulatory architecture being built under MiCA raises the question of whether European infrastructure operators will participate in or be shaped by standards set elsewhere.

*Sources: [Visa joins MAS-led project to pilot stablecoin settlement](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48300/visa-joins-mas-led-project-to-pilot-stablecoin-settlement?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Smith & Williamson hires former PSR chief Chris Hemsley**

*One of the UK's most experienced payments regulators moves into advisory practice as the PSR's agenda — from APP fraud rules to card scheme oversight — enters a pivotal phase.*

Accounting and advisory firm Smith & Williamson has appointed Chris Hemsley, the former managing director and executive board member of the Payment Systems Regulator (PSR). Hemsley also previously served as chief executive of the UK Regulators Network.

Hemsley led the PSR during a period that included the design and implementation of mandatory authorised push payment fraud reimbursement, the launch of market reviews into card scheme pricing and early work on the UK Payments Initiative. His move into advisory work comes as several of the regulatory frameworks he helped shape — including the PSR's proposed mandatory profit reporting for Visa and Mastercard — are entering consultation or implementation phases.

*Sources: [S&W appoints former Payment Systems Regulator chief Chris Hemsley](https://www.accountancytoday.co.uk/2026/08/25/sw-appoints-former-payment-systems-regulator-chief-chris-hemsley/) — Accountancy Today*
